quickAnswer: Just under two hours south of Istanbul via the Osmangazi Bridge and one hour from Bursa, İznik (ancient Nicaea) blends Roman-Byzantine city gates, the lakeside Basilica of Saint Neophytos linked to the 325 AD First Council of Nicaea, and working quartz-tile studios—ideal as a quiet day trip or paired with Bursa.

body.text: How far is İznik from Istanbul and Bursa?

İznik sits approximately 126 to 145 kilometers south of central Istanbul—a 1 hour 45 minute to 2 hour drive via the Osmangazi Bridge—and roughly 75 to 85 kilometers (about one hour by road) northeast of Bursa, making it easy to reach without domestic flights.

Travelers without a car can combine a Yalova IDO ferry from Istanbul with a connecting local minibus, or take Marmaray to Gebze followed by a taxi or regional bus, though [Istanbul-to-İznik route data](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Istanbul/%C4%B0znik) shows private driving saves two hours each way. From Bursa, [road transfers take roughly one hour](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Bursa/%C4%B0znik) across the olive-lined hills bordering Lake İznik.

body.text: What Byzantine and First Council of Nicaea sights remain?

Listed on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, İznik preserves five kilometers of Roman-Byzantine fortification walls, four monumental gates, the Hagia Sophia church (site of the 787 AD Seventh Ecumenical Council), and the shoreline Basilica of Saint Neophytos associated with early Christian Nicaea.

Emperor Constantine convened the First Council of Nicaea here in 325 AD, establishing the Nicene Creed—a milestone highlighted globally during its 1,700th anniversary in 2025. According to [UNESCO's İznik dossier](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5900/) and [KÜRE Encyclopedia's archaeological documentation](https://kureansiklopedi.com/en/detay/basilica-of-iznik-56c3d), key sites sit within a flat, walkable grid:

items: Basilica of Saint Neophytos: Discovered in 2014 just off the northeast shore and studied closely ahead of [2025 anniversary commemorations](https://www.dailysabah.com/life/religion/turkiye-basilica-rises-shedding-light-on-early-christianity), this 4th-to-5th-century three-nave basilica displays exposed stone foundations and documented opus sectile floor plans right beside the lake.

Hagia Sophia of İznik (Orhan Mosque): Standing at the ancient Roman crossroads, this basilica hosted the Seventh Ecumenical Council in 787 AD before Ottoman conversion in 1331; surviving fresco traces remain visible inside.
Lefke Gate and Istanbul Gate: Walkable stretches of double-tiered Roman and Byzantine brick-and-stone walls frame the eastern and northern town entrances.

İznik Museum (Nilüfer Hatun İmaret): Operated by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism via [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=BIZ01&DistId=MRK), this 1388 early-Ottoman soup kitchen displays Roman sarcophagi, Byzantine reliefs, and excavated 16th-century İznik kiln finds.

body.text: Where can you visit authentic hand-painted İznik tile workshops?

For genuine quartz-based çini rather than factory souvenir ceramics, visit the İznik Foundation (İznik Vakfı) workshops and independent master ateliers clustered around the 14th-century Süleyman Paşa Madrasa and town center, where skilled artisans still hand-paint and fire traditional high-quartz stonepaste tiles in small batches.

During the 16th century, İznik kilns supplied the coral-red, cobalt, and turquoise tiles lining Istanbul's Rüstem Paşa Mosque and Edirne's Selimiye Mosque. Established in 1993 and documented by the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-99949/the-objective-of-the-foundation.html), the İznik Foundation revived the lost quartz formula—a meticulous process that [University of Kansas ceramic research](https://crees.ku.edu/iznik) notes can require up to 70 days from raw quartz paste to final kiln firing. When shopping or booking a painting demonstration, ask whether the tile body is quartz (kuvars) rather than red clay, inspect the raised coral-red slip by touch, and visit independent masters working inside the courtyard of the Süleyman Paşa Madrasa.
How do you pair İznik with Bursa?

Combine İznik and Bursa into a relaxed two-day, one-night Marmara heritage loop from Istanbul: spend Day 1 walking İznik's walls, basilica, and tile ateliers with a lakeside fish lunch, then drive one hour to Bursa for its UNESCO-listed Ottoman complexes and Cumalıkızık village on Day 2.

Pairing the two cities reveals the full architectural arc from Byzantine Nicaea to the first Ottoman capital. Explore our dedicated [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) alongside [UNESCO's Bursa and Cumalıkızık World Heritage listing](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1452/) to map out the Grand Mosque (Ulu Cami), Koza Han silk market, Green Tomb (Yeşil Türbe), and timber-framed Ottoman houses in Cumalıkızık before returning to Istanbul by road or Mudanya ferry.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Istanbul to İznik?
faq.a: Driving from central Istanbul to İznik via the Osmangazi Bridge takes roughly 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours (about 126 to 145 kilometers), depending on Istanbul bridge and exit traffic.

faq.q: Can you see the underwater Basilica of Saint Neophytos in Lake İznik?
faq.a: Yes. Located just offshore near the northeastern lakeside walls, the 4th-to-5th-century basilica ruins are clearly visible from the viewing area—and receding lake levels have exposed much of the masonry above water.

faq.q: Is the Hagia Sophia of İznik open to visitors?
faq.a: Yes. The historic Byzantine church—which hosted the Seventh Ecumenical Council in 787 AD—operates today as the Orhan Mosque in the center of town and welcomes respectful visitors outside prayer times.

faq.q: How can I tell authentic quartz İznik tiles from tourist copies?
faq.a: Authentic İznik çini uses a high-quartz stonepaste body, hand-painted mineral underglazes (cobalt blue, turquoise, coral red), and a glassy transparent glaze, whereas cheap copies use standard red clay and transfer prints.

faq.q: When is the İznik Museum open?
faq.a: Housed in the 1388 Nilüfer Hatun İmaret, the İznik Museum is typically open Tuesday through Sunday and closed on Mondays; confirm seasonal hours on muze.gov.tr before traveling.

faq.q: Should I visit İznik and Bursa on the same trip?
faq.a: Yes. İznik sits about one hour northeast of Bursa, making a two-day Marmara heritage loop pairing Nicaea's Byzantine walls and tile workshops with UNESCO-listed Bursa and Cumalıkızık effortless.
